mcqs.question: What does the universal quantifier (∀) signify in a mathematical statement?

options.A: There exists at least one element in the domain for which the statement is true.
options.B: The statement is true for every element in the domain.
options.C: No element in the domain satisfies the statement.
options.D: Exactly one element in the domain satisfies the statement.

mcqs.answer: The statement is true for every element in the domain.
mcqs.explanation: The universal quantifier ∀ reads as "for all" or "for every". It asserts that the predicate holds for each element of the domain. Option A describes the existential quantifier, C describes a universal negation, and D is not a standard quantifier meaning.

mcqs.question: Which of the following best describes the meaning of the existential quantifier (∃)?

options.A: The statement holds for every element of the domain.
options.B: There exists at least one element in the domain for which the statement is true.
options.C: No element of the domain satisfies the statement.
options.D: Exactly two elements of the domain satisfy the statement.

mcqs.answer: There exists at least one element in the domain for which the statement is true.
mcqs.explanation: The existential quantifier ∃ reads as "there exists". It claims that the predicate is true for at least one element of the domain. Option A is the universal quantifier, C is the negation of an existential statement, and D is not a standard quantifier meaning.

mcqs.question: Translate the quantified statement ∀x (x > 0) into plain English.

options.A: All numbers are greater than zero.
options.B: There exists a number greater than zero.
options.C: No number is greater than zero.
options.D: Some numbers are not greater than zero.

mcqs.answer: All numbers are greater than zero.
mcqs.explanation: The universal quantifier ∀x means "for every x". The predicate "x > 0" says "x is greater than zero". Hence the whole statement reads "for every x, x is greater than zero", i.e., all numbers are greater than zero. The other options correspond to existential or negated meanings.

mcqs.question: What is the correct negation of the statement ∀x P(x)?
mcqs.explanation: Negating a universal statement ∀x P(x) yields an existential statement that there exists at least one x for which P(x) is false: ∃x ¬P(x). Option A incorrectly keeps the universal quantifier, B drops the negation, and D is equivalent to the original statement's negation but not in the standard form.

mcqs.question: Which of the following sentences correctly uses a universal quantifier?

options.A: There is a student who scored 90 marks.
options.B: Every student in the class passed the exam.

mcqs.answer: Every student in the class passed the exam.
mcqs.explanation: The phrase "Every student" translates to the universal quantifier ∀. It asserts that the predicate (passed the exam) holds for all members of the class. Option A is existential, C is also existential, and D is a negated universal but does not explicitly use the universal quantifier form.

mcqs.question: In a park, which statement correctly expresses an existential quantifier?

options.A: All birds in the park can fly.
options.B: There exists a bird in the park that cannot fly.
options.C: No bird in the park is flightless.
options.D: Every bird in the park migrates during winter.

mcqs.answer: There exists a bird in the park that cannot fly.
mcqs.explanation: The phrase "There exists" corresponds to the existential quantifier ∃, indicating at least one bird with the property of being unable to fly. Options A and D are universal statements, while C is a negated existential but does not directly use the existential form.

mcqs.question: The statement ∃x (x is even) is often misinterpreted. Which of the following is the correct translation?

options.A: There is at least one even number.

mcqs.answer: There is at least one even number.
mcqs.explanation: ∃x (x is even) means "there exists an x such that x is even", i.e., at least one even number exists. Option B describes a universal quantifier, C is the negation, and D adds an unnecessary restriction.

mcqs.question: What is the correct negation of the statement ∃x (P(x) ∧ Q(x))?

options.A: All numbers satisfy both P and Q.
options.B: There exists an x such that ¬P(x) or ¬Q(x).
options.C: For every x, if P(x) then ¬Q(x).

mcqs.explanation: Negating an existential conjunction ∃x (P(x) ∧ Q(x)) yields a universal statement that for all x, the conjunction is false: ∀x ¬(P(x) ∧ Q(x)). Option B incorrectly uses an existential quantifier, C changes the logical structure, and A is the opposite of the original statement.
